transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood CSM), Priya (CTO Lumenix), Aaron (Lead ML Eng), Nina (Procurement), Samir (Infra)

Summary/Auto notes (auto gen, may be partial):
- Ran bench compare vs incumbent for 1k token payload, showed throughput lift ~1.3x in head-to-head in our lab, P95 improved from 420ms to 345ms with tuned batching and KV cache (approx).
- Next steps: share tuned config, run 95th-percentile sweep, schedule on-prem spike.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we have about 45 minutes, i'll kick off with a quick recap of the lab runs we did this week, and then marco will go into the tuning bits, sound good?
[00:18] Priya: yeah that works, thanks, we just want to make sure the numbers are stable not one-off flukes, and also understand the tradeoffs for p95 vs sustained throughput, right.
[00:35] Marco: cool, so quick table, baseline is IncumbentVendor - that was measured on their 8-gpu cluster with default batching, our lab used rdx-small config with continuous batching and prefix kv cache enabled. fair caveats: different kernel stack, but we ran identical prompt set and same 1k token gen shape.
[01:02] Aaron: sorry can i interrupt real quick - when you say prefix kv cache, do you mean full KV caching across sessions or per-request prefix only? that was a pain point for us on the incumbent where cache invalidation caused tail spikes.
[01:17] Marco: good q - currently in the lab we used an aggressive prefix cache for repeated system prompts + user history up to 384 tokens. it's sticky per conversation id, so tera's not global, but it does reduce KV recompute on hot keys. that materially cut P95 on long sessions.
[01:44] Nina: quick procurement Q - how do you handle data retention in the hosted logs, like, can we opt out of storing prompt text? do you have SOC2 docs?
[01:58] Jasmine: yes we have SOC 2 type 2 and ISO references, i'll share the security pack after this call, also you can set retention rules or mask prompts at ingestion via our API parameter, we'll include the doc link.
[02:13] Samir: for the on-prem test i want to confirm network egress rules, we need the control plane to not phone home except to our KMS endpoints, is that supported?
[02:26] Elena: yep private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and control-plane VPC peering, we'll put the ops checklist in the repo, marco will include the on-prem spike notes.
[02:38] Marco: jumping back to numbers - in our controlled runs (50 concurrent connections, 120 qps sustained) we saw throughput 1.3x vs incumbent for the 1k token scenario, and P95 improved ~18% (baseline 420ms -> 345ms). caveat: batch sizing tuning was key — default batches were hurting small request latency.
[03:06] Priya: those are promising, can you show the delta by batch size? like what's p50/p95 for batch size 1,8,16,32?
[03:20] Marco: yes, quick summary: batch=1 p50~85ms p95~310ms, batch=8 p50~55 p95~240, batch=16 p50~60 p95~290, batch=32 throughput better but p95 climbs to ~420. so there's a sweet spot at 8 for your workload but depends on your arrival distribution.
[03:46] Aaron: hmm interesting that batch 16 p50 climbs slightly — is that due to kernel scheduling or queueing?
[03:52] Marco: mostly queueing + kv alignment overhead, we observed some long tails when KV misses lined up with larger batches. there's also quantization interplay — 4-bit quant landed better latency in some paths.
[04:12] Priya: you mentioned quantization — what's the recommended profile for our accuracy bar? we have a lot of clinical note gen and don't want hallucinations to increase.
[04:26] Marco: recommended experiment: run int8/4-bit profile with your eval prompts and compare token-level log perplexity and a small eval set for clinical hallucination metrics. in our bench the 4-bit profile kept generation quality within the noise for our open models, but recommend you validate with your golden prompt set. we'll push the profile and the eval harness.
[04:50] Jasmine: also to add — Redwood Optimize suggests per-route quant configs, so you can use higher fidelity for critical routes and aggressive quant for low-risk paths to save cost.
[05:03] Aaron: ok good, that mitigates concerns. can you also share the exact invocation flags you used in the lab? it helps us reproduce.
[05:12] Marco: yes will share runbook, kernel flags, and the perf traces — there's a link placeholder in the notes: https://redwood.example/seed-lab-runs (we'll replace with S3 link).
[05:25] Nina: on pricing, i know you have reserved capacity options, curious how it compares to the incumbent for our target qps — we need a ballpark before procurement loop.
[05:37] Jasmine: sure i can put together two options: reserved baseline for steady-state qps and burst credits for spikes; i'll include committed monthly cost and per-token marginal for bursts. expect that reserved will be materially cheaper than on-demand incumbent at your volumes. i'll send a modelled sheet.
[05:56] Priya: i want to call out one thing — our traffic has uneven diurnal spikes and occasional batch backfills overnight, so autoscaling behavior matters. did you stress test scaling up and down? we saw in the incumbent long ramp times.
[06:14] Marco: we ran a 5x step-up test; median scale time was 2.8 minutes to add nodes in our dedicated config, we also tested pre-warm policies which gave sub-60s readiness for added capacity. note: private on-prem depends on your provisioning, but the control plane supports canary pre-warm.
[06:36] Samir: for on-prem pre-warm we'd need a small always-on pool, can we do hybrid routing (hosted for burst fallback)?
[06:45] Elena: yes hybrid is common — route primary to private nodes, fallback to hosted regional pools with data egress controls, and you can set a policy for cost vs latency.
[06:58] Aaron: quick question — your P95 numbers, are they token-level or generation-complete? because our SLA needs are generation-complete for medical summaries.
[07:10] Marco: generation-complete — we measured until the final token emitted; that's what we report as P95 here.
[07:19] Priya: good to know. any regressions in output quality after the quant changes?
[07:25] Marco: minor fluctuations, we logged a few cases where formatting changed, but semantic content held. again recommend end-to-end eval with your test harness.
[07:38] Jasmine: ok pragmatic next steps — we'll send the security pack, pricing model, tuned config, and the lab runbook. we also propose an on-prem spike week where we do a live run with a subset of your data (anonymized) to validate scale and KMS integration.
[07:55] Nina: procurement would like an NDA addendum and a list of sub processors — can that be included with the security pack?
[08:05] Jasmine: yes will include that.
[08:09] Aaron: one more technical, during your benchmarking did you compare memory footprints per model variant? we have GPU memory constraints on our older machines.
[08:19] Marco: yes we included peak GPU mem numbers; the quantized variants dropped peak usage by ~30-40%, and we also have a streaming KV mode that lowers memory at the cost of a small latency penalty. will include the mem chart.
[08:36] Priya: on the incumbent comparison, are there any workload shapes where the incumbent outperforms Redwood?
[08:45] Marco: in very small token gen (<=64 tokens) with bursty single-shot traffic and no KV reuse, incumbent's micro-optimizations on their stack edged us out by ~10% p50, but once sessionality and prefix reuse kick in we have the advantage.
[09:03] Priya: that's fine, sounds like we'll want to route short single-shot traffic differently.
[09:10] Jasmine: cool, last bit — timeline, are you targeting production pilot by end of april?
[09:17] Priya: yes that timeline still stands, procurement needs pricing by next week ideally so we can start the PO cycle.
[09:25] Nina: yes procurement needs the sheet and legal stack details.
[09:29] Jasmine: we'll prioritize sending the pricing and security doc by friday (2026-03-06).
[09:34] Marco: i'll upload the tuned config and runbook by thursday (2026-03-05) and include the kernel and batch tuning notes.
[09:42] Aaron: i'll get you the traffic histogram and peak windows by monday (2026-03-09).
[09:47] Priya: ok thanks everyone, let's reconvene after the on-prem spike scheduling, after you send the artifacts we'll triage the next technical deep dive.
[09:58] Jasmine: perfect, thanks all.

(End of recording)
